To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the protein and glycosylation patterns of the synaptic junctional fractions isolated from developing rat brains change during postnatal development in a manner that correlates with changes in the morphological and functional maturation of the synapse.
the morphology, protein composition, and glycoprotein compositions of isolated synaptic junctions change during postnatal development.
isolated synaptic junctions prepared from immature brain tissues are morphologically and biochemically distinct from synaptic junctions prepared in adult animals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the developmental changes in the protein and carbohydrate composition of synaptic junctions and with the possible role of synaptic glycoproteins in synaptic development.
the biochemical and morphological characterization of the developing nervous system and the identification of molecular markers of synaptic differentiation.
the biochemical characterization of isolated synaptic junctions from immature rat brain tissues.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the synaptic junctions of developing brain differ from those of adult brain in both morphology and molecular composition.
the synaptic junctional structures isolated from immature rat brain are not functionally or morphologically identical to synaptic junctions isolated from adult brain.

the morphological and biochemical characteristics of the isolated synaptic junctional fractions are consistent with the presence of synapses in the fractions and that the changes observed during postnatal development are consistent with changes in the properties of synapses in situ.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the morphological and molecular characteristics of synaptic junctions undergo significant age-dependent changes during postnatal brain development.
the developmental changes in the protein and carbohydrate composition of synaptic junctional fractions are temporally and morphologically correlated with the development of synaptic junctions.
isolated synaptic junction fractions display age-dependent changes in morphology and protein composition during postnatal development.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the synaptic junction is a dynamic structure that changes in composition and morphology during development.
the developmental changes in synaptic junction structure and protein composition that are observed in vivo are faithfully reproduced in isolated synaptic junction fractions.
synaptic junctions isolated from immature rat brain display age-dependent changes in both morphology and protein composition.
